title: Measuring endogenous levels of unconjugated bilirubin released from isolated murine brain tissue during oxygen-glucose deprivation
protocol: Anesthetize mice with 1% sodium pentobarbital at a dose of 55 mg/kg.
Open the thoracic cavity to expose the beating heart.
Make an incision to the right atrial appendage.
Insert a 22-gauge needle into the left ventricle of the heart.
Perfuse with 20 mL of pre-oxygenated ice-cold aCSF containing enoxaparin sodium using a 20 mL syringe over 10 minutes.
Continue perfusion until the tail, limbs, and liver turn pale.
Dissect the mouse brain after successful perfusion to remove general circulation blood.
Attach the forebrain onto a specimen tray with 3M Biogel.
Fill the vibratome bath with crushed ice and pour pre-oxygenated ice-cold cutting solution into the specimen tray.
Incubate 300-μm-thick brain slices in continuously oxygenated aCSF solution at 37°C for 30 min.
Set the sectioning speed to 0.08 mm/s with 1.0 mm amplitude.
Set the vibratome frequency to 75 Hz–77 Hz.
Cut 300-μm-thickness coronal brain slices.
Collect the slices and place into a 50 mL beaker containing 10 mL aCSF.
Bubble the aCSF with oxygen continuously.
Place the beaker in a thermostat water bath at 37°C.
Incubate for 30 min for recovery.
Transfer brain slices to continuously oxygenated glucose-free aCSF (room temperature) using a trimmed pasteur pipette.
Wash the slices for 10 min to deplete remaining glucose from the extracellular space.
Transfer glucose-depleted brain slices with a bent syringe needle to a foil-wrapped, light-shielded 24-well plate.
Add 500 μL unoxygenated glucose-free aCSF (room temperature) and 3 brain slices to each well.
Turn on the hypoxic incubator and set the temperature to 37°C.
Set the control software to execute the hypoxia program (95% N2, 5% CO2).
Initiate oxygen decent stage: Continuous N2 infusion for 10 minutes to increase N2 concentration to 95%.
Maintain hypoxia sustain stage for up to 6 hours.
Collect 5 μl of glucose-free aCSF into 200 μL PCR tubes at different time points (15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 3 h, 4 h, 5 h and 6 h) for UCB concentration measurements.
Gently stir the brain slices prior to glucose-free aCSF collection to ensure even distribution of UCB into external fluid.
Store Eppendorf tubes temporarily at 4°C until use.
Avoid light exposure during aCSF’s sample collection and storage.
Mix 50 μL of 2 μM UnaG solution with 50 μL of bilirubin concentration gradient solutions in a reaction system (final UnaG concentration 1 μM).
Add 100 μL of 0.1 M PBS solution without bilirubin as blank control.
React the mixture in darkness for 10–20 min at room temperature.
Measure fluorescence intensity using microplate reader with filters for excitation and emission wavelengths at 485 and 528 nm, respectively.
Draw a standard calibration curve of fluorescence intensity against bilirubin concentration.
Detect UCB concentrations in samples at different time points.
Add 5 μL sample to 45 μL 0.1 M PBS solution and dilute 10-fold.
Mix 50 μL UnaG solution (2 μM) with 50 μL diluted UCB-containing samples for a final UnaG concentration of 1 μM and samples are diluted 20-fold.
Allow reaction in darkness for 10–20 min at room temperature.
Use microplate reader to detect the fluorescence intensity with filters for excitation and emission wavelengths at 485 and 528 nm, respectively.
